name: DINOCell: continued self-supervised DINOv2 pretraining on unlabeled cell images
what: Continues self-supervised training of a DINOv2 ViT on unlabeled cell images before supervised fine-tuning for cell instance segmentation; motivates that natural-image foundation weights are misaligned with microscopy domains.
why_better: Old plan starts from a random-init U-Net with Cellpose3 pre-annotation and pseudo-label self-training; pretraining the encoder in-domain on the unlabelled pool makes representations microscopy-specific, so with ~70 labels the downstream model converges to higher accuracy. Cause: DINOv2 fine-tuned on unlabeled cells learns cell structure; effect: +10.42% SEG over leading SAM-based models on LIVECell plus strong zero-shot on 3 OOD microscopy datasets.
evidence: LIVECell benchmark: SEG score 0.784, +10.42% over leading SAM-based models; strong zero-shot on three out-of-distribution microscopy datasets
source_title: Self-supervised Pretraining of Cell Segmentation Models
fit_small_data: high - explicitly for label-scarce cell segmentation; uses the unlabelled pool for pretraining
fit_onnx_cpu: low - ViT encoder is expensive on CPU; use as a pretraining recipe only and distill the final segmentation head into a small CNN for the desktop app
risk: Continued pretraining on a few-hundred-image pool can overfit the pool distribution; ONNX export of a ViT with 2D positional embeddings is fiddly; DINOv2 weights download size and offline constraint must be checked

name: Channel-agnostic masked autoencoder (CA-MAE) in-domain pretraining (Recursion)
what: ViT masked autoencoders pretrained in-domain on unlabeled microscopy; a channel-agnostic decoder (shared across all channels) allows different numbers/orders of input channels at inference.
why_better: Old plan has no pretraining stage at all; in-domain MAE on the unlabelled pool yields a domain-specific encoder that, combined with 70 labels, should beat random-init CNNs, and channel-agnosticity transfers to the fluorescence channels used for label checking. Cause: self-supervised objective needs zero labels; effect: MAE features beat weakly supervised baselines by up to 11.5% relative on known biological relationships and transfer across channel structures (RPI-93M -> JUMP-CP).
evidence: ViT MAEs outperform weakly supervised classifiers by up to 11.5% relative when recalling known biological relationships; CA-MAE pre-trained on RPI-93M transfers to JUMP-CP with different channel structure (CVPR 2024)
source_title: Masked Autoencoders for Microscopy are Scalable Learners of Cellular Biology
fit_small_data: high - pretraining requires only unlabelled images, which the project has in a pool
fit_onnx_cpu: medium - MAE is training-time only (runs on A5000); keep the backbone small (ViT-S/B) or fall back to the CNN variant so the deployed model stays CPU-friendly
risk: Recursion's headline gains come from 93M images; at a few-hundred-image scale the MAE encoder may add little over DINOv2 continued pretraining - pick one SSL recipe, do not do both

name: Edge-based self-supervision for semi-supervised few-shot microscopy cell segmentation
what: Combines self-supervised prediction of edge-based maps on unlabelled images with supervised training on a small labelled set for cell segmentation (MOVI 2022).
why_better: Old plan's pseudo-label self-training propagates segmentation errors into the unlabelled data; an edge self-task instead supervises unlabelled images with a geometric target that is dense, robust, and especially informative for thin 2-3 px neurites. Cause: weak signal that cannot collapse to the trivial all-background solution; effect: with only 10% of the original training set it reaches fully-annotated performance on 1- to 10-shot.
evidence: Few-shot microscopy image cell segmentation benchmark: 10% of the original training set reaches similar performance to the fully annotated database on 1- to 10-shots
source_title: Edge-Based Self-Supervision for Semi-Supervised Few-Shot Microscopy Image Cell Segmentation
fit_small_data: high - explicitly designed for the few-shot labelled regime
fit_onnx_cpu: high - CNN-based; edge head is training-time only, no extra inference cost
risk: Phase-contrast halos create bright ring 'edges' that may not coincide with true cell/neurite boundaries; validate edge targets derived from their own masks before trusting them

name: MMCS: Advanced Multi-Microscopic Views Cell Semi-supervised Segmentation
what: Semi-supervised cell segmentation trained across multiple microscope modalities using nucleus-assisted global recognition, a self-adaptive diameter filter, and temporal-ensembling (mean-teacher style).
why_better: Old plan assumes one fixed imaging domain; MMCS explicitly co-trains on varied microscope views, which directly models the PC12->SH-SY5Y and cross-microscope shifts, and temporal ensembling stabilizes pseudo-label utilization compared with plain self-training. Cause: view-diverse supervision; effect: F1 0.8239 on the NeurIPS 2022 CellSeg tuning set with limited labelled data.
evidence: NeurIPS 2022 CellSeg tuning set: F1 0.8239, within time tolerance, using less labeled multi-posture cell images from different microscopy
source_title: Advanced Multi-Microscopic Views Cell Semi-supervised Segmentation
fit_small_data: high - uses less labeled data plus unlabelled multi-view images
fit_onnx_cpu: high - U-Net-style CNN with standard ONNX export path
risk: Validated on fluorescence cell segmentation (NeurIPS 2022 CellSeg), not phase contrast; no public code stated in the paper, so re-implementation is required

name: CorrMatch: label propagation via correlation matching
what: Semi-supervised segmentation that improves pseudo-label use efficiency with two propagation strategies: pixel propagation via pairwise pixel similarities and region propagation using class-agnostic masks extracted from correlation maps.
why_better: With ~70 labelled images the bottleneck is pseudo-label quality, not backbone capacity; correlation matching mines more reliable unlabelled pixels and preserves shape information that the old plan's plain pseudo-label self-training discards. Cause: higher-precision pseudo-labels from a tiny labelled set; effect: 76%+ mIoU on Pascal VOC 2012 with only 92 annotated images - the same label budget as this project.
evidence: Pascal VOC 2012, DeepLabV3+ ResNet-101: 76%+ mIoU with only 92 annotated images
source_title: CorrMatch: Label Propagation via Correlation Matching for Semi-Supervised Semantic Segmentation
fit_small_data: high - designed for the low-labelled-data regime
fit_onnx_cpu: medium - works with a CNN backbone (use ResNet-50 or smaller for CPU); correlation matching is a training-time extra cost
risk: Benchmark is natural-image 20-class; adaptation to 2-class (soma/neurite) phase-contrast with their 70 images is unproven; region propagation assumes object-like regions and may suit neurites less than somas

name: UniMatch V2: pushing the limit of semi-supervised semantic segmentation
what: Upgraded semi-supervised framework (TPAMI 2025) inheriting weak-to-strong consistency with amplified benefit of weakly labelled data and simplified, lower-cost training versus UniMatch V1.
why_better: Replaces the old plan's plain pseudo-label self-training with the current SOTA consistency framework that extracts more signal per unlabelled image and trains cheaper than UniMatch V1. Cause: stronger consistency training with the same 70 labels + unlabelled pool; effect: reported SOTA improvements on standard SSS benchmarks (unverified numerically from abstract alone).
evidence: unverified - abstract states it improves over UniMatch while requiring less training cost; no numbers visible in the abstract retrieved
source_title: UniMatch V2: Pushing the Limit of Semi-Supervised Semantic Segmentation
fit_small_data: medium - effective with limited labels, but validated on Pascal/Cityscapes with thousands of unlabelled images; the project's unlabelled pool is much smaller
fit_onnx_cpu: medium - backbone-dependent; deploy with a lightweight CNN/UNet rather than the tested transformers
risk: Pipeline complexity (weak/strong augmentation schedules, confidence filtering, two-pass training) is non-trivial to port to a 2-class biomedical case; may not beat CorrMatch plus the edge self-task for this budget

name: BADGE: batch active learning by diverse, uncertain gradient lower bounds
what: Batch active learning that selects image sets jointly uncertain and diverse via farthest-point coreset selection on hallucinated gradient embeddings; no hand-tuned hyperparameters (ICLR 2020).
why_better: Old plan samples by entropy, which repeatedly picks similar high-entropy images (confirmation bias); BADGE's coreset geometry spreads the annotation budget across the dose x time grid (H2O2 vs doxorubicin vs curcumin at 0/6/24 h). Cause: representative + informative batches; effect: consistently as good or better than prior batch AL methods across batch sizes and architectures.
evidence: ICLR 2020: consistently performs as well or better than other batch AL approaches across batch sizes/architectures without hand-tuned hyperparameters (no single number in abstract)
source_title: Deep Batch Active Learning by Diverse, Uncertain Gradient Lower Bounds
fit_small_data: high - built for the few-label regime; gradient computation is training-time only and cheap for a U-Net
fit_onnx_cpu: high - selection runs in PyTorch; the deployed segmentation model is unchanged
risk: Gradient embeddings scale with model size (fine for U-Net, heavy for Swin); combines naturally with a topology-aware scoring term to prioritize neurite structure

name: RegAL: unified topology-aware active + semi-supervised segmentation
what: Couples sample acquisition and unlabelled-data utilization in a shared topology-aware Pareto optimization: images are selected by voxel-wise uncertainty, feature diversity, and a topological consistency metric, and stable picks feed registration-guided augmentation for a Mean Teacher student (2026).
why_better: Old plan treats entropy AL and self-training as separate objectives; RegAL adds a topological criterion, so labels are spent where branching structure is most informative and most unstable. Cause: topology-aware selection of edge cases + topology-stable augmentation; effect: outperforms state-of-the-art AL, SSL, and active semi-supervised baselines on Dice/ASD/HD95 under extreme annotation scarcity.
evidence: BraTS 2021, dHCP, ProstateX: consistently outperforms SOTA AL, SSL, and active semi-supervised baselines on Dice, ASD, HD95 under extreme scarcity (no numeric values in abstract)
source_title: Unifying Active Learning and Semi-Supervised Learning for Medical Image Segmentation
fit_small_data: high - designed for ultra-low labelled regimes
fit_onnx_cpu: medium - AL/SSL machinery is training-time only; the deployed Mean-Teacher student is a standard CNN
risk: Validated on 3D MRI volumes; porting 'topological consistency' to 2D phase-contrast fields of view (e.g., Euler characteristic / branch-count agreement on neurite masks) and diffeomorphic registration of 2D images is a real re-implementation, and no code is released

name: Class-driven scribble promotion network (scribble-based weak supervision)
what: Scribble-supervised semantic segmentation using class-aware scribble promotion, a localization rectification module, and a distance-entropy loss that adapts per-pixel confidence weights by reliability (AAAI 2024).
why_better: Drawing scribbles along neurites is orders of magnitude faster than outlining every 2-3 px tube, and cheaper to correct than Cellpose3 pre-annotations that still require full outlines. Cause: weak stroke labels scale to hundreds of images in the same time the old plan spends on 70 masks; effect: outperforms all previous scribble-supervised methods on ScribbleSup across scribble qualities, with robustness to low-quality scribbles.
evidence: ScribbleSup benchmark: outperforms all previous scribble-supervised methods with different qualities of scribble annotations (no numeric values in abstract)
source_title: Scribble Hides Class: Promoting Scribble-Based Weakly-Supervised Semantic Segmentation with Its Class Label
fit_small_data: high - scribbles are the canonical cheap label type for a 70-image budget; enables labelling 3-5x more images for the same human cost
fit_onnx_cpu: high - standard CNN/UNet model, no extra inference cost
risk: Requires a scribble annotation UI in the offline desktop app; for 2 px-wide tubes the scribble must physically cover the tube width - verify that promotion reaches the whole tube, not just the stroke, and that scribbles on somas don't bleed into neurites

name: Procedural neurite deterioration simulator (isogeometric phase-field 'digital twin')
what: Generates synthetic neurite images with controlled deterioration patterns (retraction, atrophy, fragmentation) via an isogeometric-analysis-based phase-field model, then trains MetaFormer predictors on synthetic + experimental images (2025).
why_better: Old plan has no synthetic data beyond rigid copy-paste; a procedural simulator produces exactly the toxin-induced morphologies the NTI measures (length loss, branch loss, fragmentation) with perfect ground truth, so segmentation and morphometry are trained on the full toxicity spectrum without additional labels. Cause: unlimited label-perfect data spanning dose/time states; effect: average errors of 1.96% on synthetic and 6.03% on experimental neurite deterioration.
evidence: Average errors 1.9641% (synthetic) and 6.0339% (experimental) neurite deterioration with MetaFormer spatiotemporal attention model
source_title: High-throughput digital twin framework for predicting neurite deterioration using MetaFormer attention
fit_small_data: high - synthetic data is label-free and unbounded
fit_onnx_cpu: high - the generator is a training-time tool; the inference model is a small CNN
risk: Building a phase-field simulator for 2D PC12 morphology inside the 15-week window is substantial; cheaper fallback is a branching process (random-walk / diffusion-limited aggregation) parameterized by measured branch-angle distributions; the domain gap to phase-contrast rendering (halos, background haze) must be explicitly modelled or the simulator creates a sim-to-real gap

name: Domain-randomized deep learning (DRDL) for neuroimage analysis
what: IEEE Signal Processing Magazine (2025) tutorial on synthesis-driven training: render synthetic images from anatomical segmentation maps with randomized intensities and content so models generalize to image types unseen during training, without retraining or fine-tuning.
why_better: Old plan's rigid copy-paste + histogram matching covers only geometric and simple photometric shifts; DRDL randomizes full appearance from the 70 masks, so the model learns invariance to exactly the appearance axes where PC12 vs SH-SY5Y and microscope-to-microscope differ. Cause: structure and appearance are decoupled during training; effect: generalization across unseen modalities/microscopes demonstrated in microscopy (among MRI, CT, PET, OCT, ultrasound, EM, X-ray).
evidence: Qualitative review evidence: demonstrated across MRI, CT, PET, OCT, ultrasound, electron and fluorescence microscopy, and X-ray microtomography; trade-off is increased computational demands
source_title: Domain-randomized deep learning for neuroimage analysis
fit_small_data: high - synthesis multiplies the 70 masks into many appearance variants for free
fit_onnx_cpu: high - synthesis is training-time only; the deployed model is a standard CNN
risk: Faithful phase-contrast rendering (halo/diffraction-ring physics) is non-trivial; start with photometric + blur/PSF randomization and only add physical rendering if the simple version leaves cross-microphone error

name: ROID: universal test-time adaptation (weight ensembling, diversity weighting, prior correction)
what: Online test-time adaptation framework covering domain non-stationarity and temporal correlation: certainty/diversity weighting against trivial solutions, continual source-adapted weight averaging against catastrophic forgetting, and adaptive class-prior correction (WACV 2024).
why_better: Old plan freezes the model after training and uses the 5-seed ensemble only for uncertainty; ROID lets the deployed model re-tune itself to a new well, microscope, or cell line at test time with no labels. Cause: adaptation to the actual test distribution; effect: improved accuracy under sequential domain shifts where plain entropy minimization (Tent) degrades via bias, forgetting, or prior shift.
evidence: unverified - claims new standards in the universal TTA field across a wide range of settings, datasets, and models (WACV 2024); no numbers in the abstract retrieved
source_title: Universal Test-time Adaptation through Weight Ensembling, Diversity Weighting, and Prior Correction
fit_small_data: high - test-time only; requires no additional labels
fit_onnx_cpu: medium - needs a few backprop steps at inference (PyTorch, not pure ONNX Runtime); acceptable if adaptation runs offline per field of view rather than interactively
risk: Entropy-based TTA can drift on low-diversity batches (single dish/well); gate adaptation on the method's own diversity criterion or fall back to batch-norm recalibration only (Tent-style)

name: AURA-net: robust phase-contrast segmentation with few annotations
what: CNN with attention mechanisms, transfer learning, and an active-contour-inspired loss tailored to phase-contrast microscopy, trained on datasets of fewer than 100 images (ISBI 2021).
why_better: Old plan's U-Net baseline is a generic CNN with CE+Dice that treats phase-contrast halos as ordinary texture; AURA-net's boundary-aware loss and attention model the halo/edge-brightness signature explicitly. Cause: loss matches phase-contrast imaging physics; effect: outperforms state-of-the-art alternatives on several <100-image datasets - the same label budget as this project's 70 images.
evidence: Several small datasets (<100 images each): outperforms state-of-the-art alternatives (no numeric values in abstract)
source_title: aura-net: robust segmentation of phase-contrast microscopy images with few annotations
risk: 2021 paper; the two transferable ideas (active-contour-inspired loss + attention) are small, cheap additions to the existing U-Net - low-risk quick win, but no public code was found in the retrieved abstract

name: muMatch: foundation models for semi-supervised learning and domain adaptation (EM, incl. neurites)
what: Student-teacher semi-supervised framework built on frozen vision foundation models (SAM, SAM2, DINOv2/v3) with domain adaptation, evaluated on challenging EM tasks including mitochondrion, nucleus, and neurite segmentation (2026).
why_better: Old plan uses Cellpose/SAM only as one-shot pre-annotation; muMatch shows foundation models can act as persistent pseudo-label providers inside a student-teacher loop, so every unlabelled image is mined repeatedly as the student improves. Cause: foundation-model features + iterative refinement; effect: consistent improvements over strong baselines including on neurite segmentation, with reduced annotation effort.
evidence: consistent improvements over strong baselines on EM mitochondrion, nucleus, and neurite segmentation tasks (no numeric values in abstract)
source_title: muMatch: Foundation Models for Semi-supervised Learning and Domain Adaptation in EM
fit_small_data: high - semi-supervised regime with few labels is exactly the 70-image setting
fit_onnx_cpu: low - SAM/DINOv2 forward passes are heavy on CPU; use foundation models only for offline pseudo-label generation and keep the student a small CNN for desktop inference
risk: Validated on electron microscopy, not phase-contrast light microscopy - a large domain gap; treat as a recipe (frozen DINOv2/SAM teacher, small-CNN student, consistency training) rather than a drop-in model
